memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen-the entire army of
Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
But the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on
their right and on their left." - Ex 14:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter places these two sentences side by side deliberately.

Not one Egyptian survived. Not one Israelite was lost. The same sea, the same
night, two completely opposite outcomes. The difference was not skill or
strength. Egypt was far stronger. The difference was whose side God was on and
who had been covered by the blood on the doorframe.

Notice that verse 29 repeats verse 22 almost word for word. Scripture pauses to
say it again: they went through on dry ground, walls of water either side. God
wants the picture fixed in our minds.

Israel's complete safety was not because they were brave or faithful. They had
spent the previous evening accusing Moses of bringing them out to die. Their
rescue rested entirely on God.

That is deeply comforting. The people God saved that night were frightened,
complaining, and unimpressive. He saved them anyway, completely, not losing one.

Jesus said of those the Father gave Him, "I shall lose none of all those he has
given me" (John 6:39). The One who brought Israel through the sea without losing
a single person keeps His people still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God's keeping of you depends on your performance?
2. What does "not one lost" mean for your assurance today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You brought Your people through without losing one. Hold
me securely, not because I am strong, but because You are. Amen.
